# Example Output — Email Address Obfuscation

*Generated by applying the Email Address Obfuscation skill to `example-input.md`.*

---

## 1. Address inventory

| Occurrence | Location | Treatment |
|---|---|---|
| `hello@example.com` anchor | contact page | XOR-hex span + decoder |
| `hello@example.com` footer link | all 5 pages | XOR-hex span + decoder (per-instance payloads) |
| `support@example.com` error string | `/account/reset-password` JS | runtime `['support','example.com'].join('@')` |
| `hello@example.com` | `email-templates/welcome.html` | legitimately plain — unlinked from docs page, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex` route added |

Interim note: with no contact form yet, the obfuscated mailto is the primary channel; revisit when the form ships next quarter.

## 2. Implementation

- Each occurrence becomes `<span class="obf-email" data-e="<xor-hex payload>"></span>`; the first payload byte is the XOR key, so every instance carries its own random key — six payloads for `hello@`, all different, all decoding identically.
- `/scripts/email-decode.js` (external, same-origin) rebuilds a normal `<a href="mailto:...">` in each span at load. **CSP unchanged** — `script-src 'self'` already permits it.
- Every span carries `<noscript>hello [at] example [dot] com</noscript>` — screen-reader and no-JS visitors still get the address.
- The reset-page error string now assembles at runtime; the literal no longer exists in the served file.

## 3. Verification log

**Per-payload decode check (before deploy):** all 7 payloads round-tripped through the decode one-liner to the exact intended address — none hand-written; two were copied verbatim from the already-shipped contact page.

**Live sweep (after deploy):**

```
for p in / /services /about /contact /account/reset-password; do
  curl -s https://www.example.com$p | grep -c "hello@example.com\|support@example.com"
done
→ 0 for every page and for /scripts/*.js
```

## 4. Residual plain addresses

- `email-templates/welcome.html` — must contain the plain address (it is the artefact being sent). Now unlinked from the docs page and served with `noindex`; noted in the operator docs as the one intentional plain occurrence.
